title: BBC Learning English from the News 2025 — Quiz 12
description: Choose the best answer for each question about vocabulary and usage.

elements.name: q111_frontrunner
elements.title: Having led every poll, the candidate is considered the ___ for the nomination.

elements.name: q112_dwindling
elements.title: Which sentence uses “dwindling” correctly?
choices: The balloon kept dwindling as it filled with air.
Our dwindling supplies will soon run out.
Dwindling attendance meant more people came every week.
The dwindling pile grew taller each day.
elements.correctAnswer: Our dwindling supplies will soon run out.

elements.name: q113_smuggle
elements.title: The officers found that someone had tried to ___ expensive goods across the border without declaring them.

elements.name: q114_turn_the_corner
elements.title: After losing money for months, the business finally began to ___ when orders recovered.

elements.name: q115_tumble
elements.title: The stack began to ___ when someone pulled out the bottom box.

elements.name: q116_spar
elements.title: The two commentators often ___ over policy, exchanging sharp arguments on air.

elements.name: q117_game_of_chicken
elements.title: Both managers threatened to resign and waited to see who would back down first. It became ___.

elements.name: q118_rubble
elements.title: After the building collapsed, workers cleared the ___ from the road.

elements.name: q119_cling
elements.title: The child continued to ___ to the railing, gripping it tightly.

elements.name: q120_deepen_crisis
elements.title: Cutting emergency funding would ___ the crisis by making help even harder to obtain.
